_note: Nodes retired from the corpus on 2026-08-29 as confirmed duplicates, merged into the surviving id shown. Full original records preserved verbatim so the merge is reversible: paste the record back into its original slice file and repoint the edges. A second batch was retired the same day as a modelling decision: treaty, trade-agreement, investment-treaty-network, multilateral-convention and membership/relationship-framing nodes, none of which is a statistical publication with a methodology dependency. All were orphans — no edge was broken. Full records preserved verbatim so the decision is reversible. A third, much smaller batch was retired the same day: analytical meta-nodes — comparison frameworks and policy postures with no publication behind them. Deliberately kept SMALL: "framing" turned out to be a Grok verbal tic that appears in the titles and descriptions of perfectly real statistics nodes, and the corpus's own "meta-node" phrasing describes a node's role in the graph rather than its nature, so neither is a safe signal to sweep on.

The EU is Türkiye’s largest trade partner by a wide margin (roughly 40%+ of exports and a large share of imports). Continuously cited in trade, industrial and accession analysis.
record._notes: Foundational external-trade architecture node. Highest-centrality bilateral frame for Turkey.
record._url_evidence: EUR-Lex page confirms Decision No 1/95 of the EC-Turkey Association Council 'on implementing the final phase of the Customs Union', adopted 22 Dec 1995, in force 31 Dec 1995 - the underlying legal instrument for this framing node.
record._cadence_evidence: EUR-Lex CELEX 21996D0213(01) is Decision No 1/95 of the EC-Turkey Association Council on implementing the final phase of the Customs Union, adopted 22 December 1995, in force 31 December 1995 - a single legal act.

record.title: Türkiye free trade agreement network framing
record.publisher: Ministry of Trade / related
record.description: Overall framing of Türkiye’s network of free trade agreements and preferential arrangements beyond the EU Customs Union. No publication cycle.

record.title: Türkiye–EFTA Free Trade Agreement

record.title: Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) — legal instrument

record.title: EU–Taiwan Trade and Investment Dialogue (TID)
record.publisher: European Commission / Taiwan authorities (via representative offices)
record.description: Regular high-level dialogue on trade, investment, economic security and critical value chains (including semiconductors). The EU is a major source of FDI into Taiwan and an important destination for Taiwanese investment; the Dialogue is the principal institutional channel for managing that relationship in the absence of a formal FTA or BIA.
record._notes: Major non-US, non-China institutional channel. Raises Taiwan’s top-level connectivity by giving the EU a formal recurring node rather than leaving the relationship implicit.
_referenced_by: Broader Taiwan FTA/ECA and dialogue network
record._cadence_evidence: European Commission trade-policy news: 'EU and Taiwan hold fourth Trade and Investment Dialogue' (12 December 2025), with earlier dialogue news items dated 2 June 2022 and December 2024 — four dialogues over roughly four years, i.e. about one per year. The page itself states only that exchanges will continue, with no fixed schedule.

record.title: Agreement between New Zealand and the Separate Customs Territory of Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu on Economic Cooperation (ANZTEC)
record.publisher: Taiwan and New Zealand
record.description: Comprehensive economic cooperation agreement that entered into force in 2013. One of the higher-quality bilateral instruments Taiwan has concluded with a developed economy.
record._notes: High-standard bilateral FTA. Supports the trade-agreement cluster.
record._url_evidence: International Trade Administration ECA/FTA portal page on ANZTEC: signed 10 July 2013, in force 1 December 2013, 25 chapters, tariff liberalisation shares.

record._notes: Complements ANZTEC as a core high-quality bilateral instrument.

record.title: Taiwan’s FTA / ECA network overview

US Taiwan policy and economic-security documents

record._url_evidence: American Institute in Taiwan page carrying the full text of the Taiwan Relations Act (Public Law 96-8), all 18 sections.

record.title: Vietnam FTA / EPA network overview
record.publisher: Derived from trade-policy sources
record.description: System-level view of Vietnam’s extensive FTA network (ASEAN, CPTPP, EVFTA, RCEP, bilateral agreements with Japan, Korea, etc.). Organises the individual treaty nodes and underpins export diversification.
record._notes: High-level trade-architecture organising node.
record._url_evidence: Vietnam's official FTA Portal (MOIT), which enumerates the country's agreements: EVFTA, CPTPP, UKVFTA, VIFTA, VN-UAE CEPA, RCEP, VKFTA, VJEPA, ASEAN+ FTAs and the WTO agreement.
record._cadence_evidence: fta.gov.vn is a live portal: searchable HS-code tariff-preference lookup across 16+ agreements plus rolling news; the page states no release frequency and has no discrete edition.
record.cadence_note: Continuously updated database/portal with no discrete editions. The number is the renderer convention decided 2026-08-18 (HANDOFF section 7) and applied 2026-08-19: a nominal releases_per_year so that absence keeps meaning 'one-off instrument' only - 250 encodes business-day updating (the live corpus's daily-FX convention), 365 genuinely all-days monitoring. It is a statement of continuous flow for the pulse/beam system, not a claim of counted editions - the observed reality is in _cadence_evidence.

record.title: Vietnam–China Comprehensive Strategic Partnership framing

record.title: Defence and security policy framing (archipelagic posture)
record.publisher: Ministry of Defence / related strategic documents

record._cadence_evidence: The cited document is the Buku Putih Pertahanan Indonesia 2008 (18 Feb 2008), which states it updates the 2003 white paper 'Mempertahankan Tanah Air Memasuki Abad XXI' - two editions five years apart, i.e. roughly one per five years.

record.title: Prefectural statistical contrast framework (Tokyo vs Okinawa / peripheral)
record.publisher: Various (Tokyo Metropolitan Government, Okinawa Prefecture, Cabinet Office Prefectural Accounts)
record.description: Conceptual and data framework that systematically compares Tokyo Metropolitan Accounts / Yearbook with peripheral prefectural yearbooks (exemplified by Okinawa) and the full set of Prefectural Accounts. Used to test hierarchy homogeneity and to surface regional heterogeneity in income, industry structure, demography and social indicators.
record._notes: Meta-node that makes the regional contrast explicit. Japan’s statistical system is highly decentralised at the prefectural level; the Tokyo–Okinawa (and broader core–periphery) comparison is the practical test of whether the same hierarchy of reports exists and how much independent local production occurs. Supports the homogeneity-check principle in the country strategy.
_referenced_by: Tokyo Metropolitan Accounts and Statistical Yearbook
Cabinet Office Annual Report on Prefectural Accounts
National accounts regional analysis and fiscal equalisation studies
record._url_evidence: Cabinet Office ESRI 県民経済計算 (Prefectural Accounts) series landing page, fetched and confirmed: lists statistical tables by prefecture for FY2008-2023, methodology/terminology notes and links to individual prefectures' own publication pages. Note: the item as titled is a synthesised cross-publisher framework rather than a single publication; this is the Cabinet Office Prefectural Accounts component named in its publisher field, and no single official page exists for the Tokyo/Okinawa contrast framework itself.

record.title: Extended regional contrast (Seoul Capital Area vs non-capital provinces / GRDP + demographic differentials)
record.publisher: Statistics Korea / local governments
record.description: Synthesised framework that systematically compares the Seoul Capital Area with other provinces and metropolitan cities using GRDP, population, ageing, fertility, employment and housing indicators. Tests hierarchy homogeneity and surfaces core–periphery differentials.
record._notes: Meta-node that operationalises the regional-contrast principle for Korea. Extreme concentration in the Seoul Capital Area is a defining structural feature; explicit comparison with peripheral provinces (e.g., Jeolla, Gyeongsang, Gangwon, Jeju) strengthens the graph’s ability to capture spatial inequality and policy responses.
_referenced_by: Population Census and Vital Statistics regional tables
Housing and labour statistics by province
record._url_evidence: Retrieved KOSIS 'e-지방지표' (e-Local/Regional Indicators), Statistics Korea's official regional indicator service; the page's indicator tree contains 1인당 GRDP and 1인당 지역총소득, 고령인구비율/노령화지수, 합계출산율, 고용률 and 주택보급률/주택소유율, with 시도별 상황판, 테마별 상황판 and 복합 비교 dashboards for comparing provinces and metropolitan cities.

record.title: New Southbound Policy — technology and semiconductor diplomacy components
record.publisher: Executive Yuan / related ministries
record.description: Policy framework that leverages Taiwan’s semiconductor, AI and trusted-industry strengths to deepen economic and technology ties with Southeast Asian and South Asian partners, thereby diversifying international space.
record._notes: Diversification node that complements the US-centric economic-security architecture. Uses the same semiconductor/AI assets to expand Taiwan’s international economic space.
_referenced_by: Outbound investment and trade statistics with Southbound partners
record._url_evidence: Retrieved and read. Executive Yuan policy page 'Xin nanxiang zhengce tuidong jihua' (New Southbound Policy Promotion Plan) in the Executive Yuan's key-policies section. Confirmed content includes the 18 target countries across ASEAN, South Asia and Australasia, the shift from a one-way manufacturing-base relationship to reciprocal partnership, and specifically the technology/industry components the node describes: taking the five major innovative industries into partner markets (IoT/ETC, smart healthcare, smart campus), overseas export cooperation platforms for infrastructure and turnkey projects, technology exchange platforms, and strengthening cross-border linkage through science parks and research institutions. NOTE: this is a policy framework document, not a statistical product. MOFA's nspp.mofa.gov.tw still returns nothing readable.
record._url_route: Executive Yuan main site (ey.gov.tw) instead of the unreadable nspp.mofa.gov.tw
record._cadence_evidence: The Executive Yuan page is the 新南向政策推動計畫 policy document dated 105-09-26 (26 September 2016) — a single approved policy plan with no stated revision cycle; later items are separate news releases.
